items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Al Rose told me something the other night.

ctx.x: Well, no. You see what happens here, I'll tell you. It seems like everything else. And this racial affairs that we have right now, that the colored people are trying to imitate the white. Just the opposite of what the other people face. In place of keeping to their own style, they're trying to imitate the white. And imitation is bad and it's no good. Because you never can be the original. I don't care how good you are, you'll never beat the original.

Al, just let me digress one moment. Al Rose told me something the other night. You know how much these Japanese boys over here, how much they imitate the George Lewis band. And that clarinet player thinks George, of course, is the most wonderful thing in the world. And just to show you how far imitation can go sometimes, he had a bottle of Dr. Tishner's antiseptic, you know, in his clarinet case. And somebody asked him, why in the world are you carrying a bottle of Dr. Tishner's in your clarinet case? What's it…

No, we're going right back to where we started from. Now we're speaking about rhythm, tempo, kick, swing. You understand? Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. Now, the people, intelligent people are broad-minded. It's only but the ignorant people that never sits down to try to figure this out. But if the intelligent people, if they just sit down and figure this out for themselves, they're going to find out that I'm telling you the truth. Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: there was also a session that was called Doc and His Patience with the two clarinets, Raymond Burke and Harry Shields, and Jeanette Kimball on piano, and there was also a tuba and a bass on that, Chink Martin and Sherwood and Japanic.

ctx.x: Joe Moritz, who did I insult the most?

Well we did a session with Joe Avery and Louis Barbrun, or Paul Barbrun, excuse me, and a session with Sweet Emma and Percy Humphrey, and of course there was the session that was called Doc and His Patience with the two clarinets, Raymond Burke and Harry Shields, and Jeanette Kimball on piano, and there was also a tuba and a bass on that, Chink Martin and Sherwood and Japanic. Johnny St. Cyril.
What do you think of a soprano sax as an instrument?
